sanskrit: tasyāvarjitanāgasya kārṣṇiḥ parapuraṃjayaḥ rājño rajatapuṅkhena bhallenāpaharac chiraḥ
english: As that king's elephant was brought low, the son of Kṛṣṇa, conqueror of hostile cities, struck off the king's head with a silver-feathered broad-arrow.

sanskrit: vigāhya tad gajānīkaṃ bhīmaseno 'pi pāṇḍavaḥ vyacarat samare mṛdnan gajān indro girīn iva
english: Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava too, plunging into that host of elephants, ranged across the battle crushing the beasts as Indra shatters mountains.

sanskrit: ekaprahārābhihatān bhīmasenena kuñjarān apaśyāma raṇe tasmin girīn vajrahatān iva
english: In that battle we saw elephants felled by Bhīmasena with a single blow, like mountains smitten by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: bhagnadantān bhagnakaṭān bhagnasakthāṃś ca vāraṇān bhagnapṛṣṭhān bhagnakumbhān nihatān parvatopamān
english: There lay the elephants slain, their tusks broken, their temples broken, their thighs broken, their backs broken, their frontal globes broken — each like a fallen mountain.

sanskrit: nadataḥ sīdataś cānyān vimukhān samare gajān vimūtrān bhagnasaṃvignāṃs tathā viśakṛto 'parān
english: Other elephants we saw bellowing and sinking down, turning their backs upon the fight, voiding urine, shattered and panic-stricken, and yet others loosing their dung in terror.

sanskrit: bhīmasenasya mārgeṣu gatāsūn parvatopamān apaśyāma hatān nāgān niṣṭanantas tathāpare
english: Along Bhīmasena's paths we saw slain elephants huge as mountains, their life-breath gone, while still others lay groaning.

sanskrit: vamanto rudhiraṃ cānye bhinnakumbhā mahāgajāḥ vihvalanto gatā bhūmiṃ śailā iva dharātale
english: And other great elephants, their frontal globes split, vomiting blood, reeling, sank to the earth like crags toppling upon the ground.

sanskrit: medorudhiradigdhāṅgo vasāmajjāsamukṣitaḥ vyacarat samare bhīmo daṇḍapāṇir ivāntakaḥ
english: His limbs smeared with fat and blood, drenched in marrow and grease, Bhīma ranged across the battle like Death himself, rod in hand.

sanskrit: gajānāṃ rudhirāktāṃ tāṃ gadāṃ bibhrad vṛkodaraḥ ghoraḥ pratibhayaś cāsīt pinākīva pinākadhṛk
english: Bearing that mace reddened with the blood of elephants, Vṛkodara was terrible and dreadful, like the wielder of the Pināka bearing his bow.

sanskrit: nirmathyamānāḥ kruddhena bhīmasenena dantinaḥ sahasā prādravañ śiṣṭā mṛdnantas tava vāhinīm
english: Churned by the wrathful Bhīmasena, the surviving tuskers fled headlong, trampling your own army as they went.

sanskrit: taṃ hi vīraṃ maheṣvāsāḥ saubhadrapramukhā rathāḥ paryarakṣanta yudhyantaṃ vajrāyudham ivāmarāḥ
english: That hero, as he fought, the great bowmen and charioteers led by the son of Subhadrā guarded round about, as the immortals guard the wielder of the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: śoṇitāktāṃ gadāṃ bibhrad ukṣito gajaśoṇitaiḥ kṛtānta iva raudrātmā bhīmaseno vyadṛśyata
english: Bearing his blood-stained mace, drenched in the blood of elephants, Bhīmasena appeared, fierce of spirit, like the Ender of all things.

sanskrit: vyāyacchamānaṃ gadayā dikṣu sarvāsu bhārata nṛtyamānam apaśyāma nṛtyantam iva śaṃkaram
english: As he wielded his mace and strove in every quarter, O Bhārata, we saw him dancing as though it were Śaṃkara himself who danced.

sanskrit: yamadaṇḍopamāṃ gurvīm indrāśanisamasvanām apaśyāma mahārāja raudrāṃ viśasanīṃ gadām
english: We beheld, O great king, that fierce and slaughtering mace, heavy as the rod of Yama, ringing like the thunderbolt of Indra.

sanskrit: vimiśrāṃ keśamajjābhiḥ pradigdhāṃ rudhireṇa ca pinākam iva rudrasya kruddhasyābhighnataḥ paśūn
english: Clotted with hair and marrow and smeared with blood, it was like the Pināka of the wrathful Rudra as he strikes down living creatures.

sanskrit: yathā paśūnāṃ saṃghātaṃ yaṣṭyā pālaḥ prakālayet tathā bhīmo gajānīkaṃ gadayā paryakālayat
english: As a herdsman drives a gathered flock before him with his staff, so did Bhīma drive the host of elephants before him with his mace.

sanskrit: gadayā vadhyamānās te mārgaṇaiś ca samantataḥ svāny anīkāni mṛdnantaḥ prādravan kuñjarās tava
english: Battered by his mace and by arrows on every side, your tuskers fled, trampling down your own divisions as they went.

sanskrit: mahāvāta ivābhrāṇi vidhamitvā sa vāraṇān atiṣṭhat tumule bhīmaḥ śmaśāna iva śūlabhṛt
english: Having scattered the elephants as a great wind scatters the clouds, Bhīma stood firm amid the tumult, like the trident-bearer in his burning-ground.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmin hate gajānīke putro duryodhanas tava bhīmasenaṃ ghnatety evaṃ sarvasainyāny acodayat
english: Saṃjaya said: When that host of elephants had been destroyed, your son Duryodhana urged on all his troops, crying, "Slay Bhīmasena!"

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāṇy anīkāni tava putrasya śāsanāt abhyadravan bhīmasenaṃ nadantaṃ bhairavān ravān
english: Then, at your son's command, all the divisions rushed upon Bhīmasena, who roared aloud with terrible cries.

sanskrit: taṃ balaugham aparyantaṃ devair api durutsaham āpatantaṃ suduṣpāraṃ samudram iva parvaṇi
english: That boundless flood of force, hard for even the gods to withstand, came rushing upon him, well-nigh impassable, like the sea swelling at the full moon.

sanskrit: rathanāgāśvakalilaṃ śaṅkhadundubhināditam athānantam apāraṃ ca narendrastimitahradam
english: Thronged with chariots, elephants, and horses, resounding with conch and kettledrum, endless and shoreless, with kings for its still deep pools —

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmasenaḥ samare mahodadhim ivāparam senāsāgaram akṣobhyaṃ veleva samavārayat
english: that unshakable ocean of an army, like a second mighty deep, Bhīmasena held back in battle as the shore holds back the sea.

sanskrit: tad āścaryam apaśyāma śraddheyam api cādbhutam bhīmasenasya samare rājan karmātimānuṣam
english: We beheld there a marvel, O king, credible yet wondrous — the more-than-human feat of Bhīmasena in battle.

sanskrit: udīrṇāṃ pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ sāśvāṃ sarathakuñjarām asaṃbhramaṃ bhīmaseno gadayā samatāḍayat
english: The whole surging earth, with its horses, its chariots, and its elephants, Bhīmasena smote with his mace, undismayed.

sanskrit: sa saṃvārya balaughāṃs tān gadayā rathināṃ varaḥ atiṣṭhat tumule bhīmo girir merur ivācalaḥ
english: Having stayed those floods of force with his mace, Bhīma, foremost of car-warriors, stood firm amid the tumult, unmoving as Mount Meru.

sanskrit: tasmin sutumule ghore kāle paramadāruṇe bhrātaraś caiva putrāś ca dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca pārṣataḥ
english: In that terrible and most dreadful hour of utmost tumult, his brothers and his sons, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna the son of Pṛṣata,

sanskrit: draupadeyābhimanyuś ca śikhaṇḍī ca mahārathaḥ na prājahan bhīmasenaṃ bhaye jāte mahābalam
english: and the sons of Draupadī and Abhimanyu, and Śikhaṇḍin the great car-warrior — these did not forsake the mighty Bhīmasena, though terror had arisen.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaikyāyasīṃ gurvīṃ pragṛhya mahatīṃ gadām avadhīt tāvakān yodhān daṇḍapāṇir ivāntakaḥ pothayan rathavṛndāni vājivṛndāni cābhibhūḥ
english: Then, seizing his great heavy mace of wrought iron, he slew your warriors like Death rod in hand, the conqueror smashing the throngs of chariots and the throngs of horses.

sanskrit: vyacarat samare bhīmo yugānte pāvako yathā vinighnan samare sarvān yugānte kālavad vibhuḥ
english: Bhīma ranged across the battle like the fire at the end of an age, striking down all before him, mighty as Time at the dissolution of the world.

sanskrit: ūruvegena saṃkarṣan rathajālāni pāṇḍavaḥ pramardayan gajān sarvān naḍvalānīva kuñjaraḥ
english: Dragging tangles of chariots along by the rush of his thighs, the Pāṇḍava crushed all the elephants as a tusker crushes beds of reeds.

sanskrit: mṛdnan rathebhyo rathino gajebhyo gajayodhinaḥ sādinaś cāśvapṛṣṭhebhyo bhūmau caiva padātinaḥ
english: He smote the car-warriors from their chariots, the elephant-fighters from their elephants, the horsemen from the backs of their steeds, and the foot-soldiers down upon the ground.

sanskrit: tatra tatra hataiś cāpi manuṣyagajavājibhiḥ raṇāṅgaṇaṃ tad abhavan mṛtyor āghātasaṃnibham
english: With men and elephants and horses slain here and there, that field of battle became like the very slaughter-house of Death.

sanskrit: pinākam iva rudrasya kruddhasyābhighnataḥ paśūn yamadaṇḍopamām ugrām indrāśanisamasvanām dadṛśur bhīmasenasya raudrāṃ viśasanīṃ gadām
english: Like the Pināka of the wrathful Rudra as he strikes down living creatures — fierce, like the rod of Yama, ringing like the thunderbolt of Indra — men beheld the dreadful, slaughtering mace of Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: āvidhyato gadāṃ tasya kaunteyasya mahātmanaḥ babhau rūpaṃ mahāghoraṃ kālasyeva yugakṣaye
english: As the great-souled son of Kuntī whirled his mace, his form blazed forth most terrible, like that of Time at the ending of an age.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā mahatīṃ senāṃ drāvayantaṃ punaḥ punaḥ dṛṣṭvā mṛtyum ivāyāntaṃ sarve vimanaso 'bhavan
english: Seeing him thus routing that mighty host again and again, coming on like Death itself, all grew downcast in spirit.

sanskrit: yato yataḥ prekṣate sma gadām udyamya pāṇḍavaḥ tena tena sma dīryante sarvasainyāni bhārata
english: Wherever the Pāṇḍava looked as he raised his mace, in that very quarter all the troops were rent asunder, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: pradārayantaṃ sainyāni balaughenāparājitam grasamānam anīkāni vyāditāsyam ivāntakam
english: He clove the armies apart, unconquered amid that flood of force, devouring the divisions like the gaping-mouthed Ender.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā bhīmakarmāṇaṃ pragṛhītamahāgadam dṛṣṭvā vṛkodaraṃ bhīṣmaḥ sahasaiva samabhyayāt
english: Seeing Vṛkodara thus terrible in his deeds, his great mace upraised, Bhīṣma straightway rushed against him.

sanskrit: mahatā meghaghoṣeṇa rathenādityavarcasā chādayañ śaravarṣeṇa parjanya iva vṛṣṭimān
english: With his chariot loud as a great thundercloud and bright as the sun, he covered him with a rain of arrows, like the rain-laden cloud-god pouring down his showers.

sanskrit: tam āyāntaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā vyāttānanam ivāntakam bhīṣmaṃ bhīmo mahābāhuḥ pratyudīyād amarṣaṇaḥ
english: Seeing him come on thus, like Death with gaping jaws, the mighty-armed Bhīma, brooking no rival, went forth to meet Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: tasmin kṣaṇe sātyakiḥ satyasaṃdhaḥ; śinipravīro 'bhyapatat pitāmaham nighnann amitrān dhanuṣā dṛḍhena; sa kampayaṃs tava putrasya senām
english: In that moment Sātyaki, true to his pledge, the hero of Śini's line, fell upon the grandsire, smiting down his foes with his stout bow and making your son's army tremble.

sanskrit: taṃ yāntam aśvai rajataprakāśaiḥ; śarān dhamantaṃ dhanuṣā dṛḍhena nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ tadānīṃ; sarve gaṇā bhārata ye tvadīyāḥ
english: As he came on with steeds gleaming like silver, hurling arrows from his stout bow, none of your own troops, O Bhārata, could turn him back in that hour.

sanskrit: avidhyad enaṃ niśitaiḥ śarāgrair; alambuso rājavarārśyaśṛṅgiḥ taṃ vai caturbhiḥ pratividhya vīro; naptā śiner abhyapatad rathena
english: Alambusa, son of Ṛśyaśṛṅga, pierced him with the points of sharp arrows; but the hero, the grandson of Śini, struck back at him with four and bore down upon him with his chariot.

sanskrit: anvāgataṃ vṛṣṇivaraṃ niśamya; madhye ripūṇāṃ parivartamānam prāvartayantaṃ kurupuṃgavāṃś ca; punaḥ punaś ca praṇadantam ājau
english: Marking the best of the Vṛṣṇis come on, wheeling about in the midst of his foes, putting to flight the bulls of the Kurus and roaring again and again in the fray —

sanskrit: nāśaknuvan vārayituṃ variṣṭhaṃ; madhyaṃdine sūryam ivātapantam na tatra kaś cinn aviṣaṇṇa āsīd; ṛte rājan somadattasya putrāt
english: none could check that peerless warrior, blazing like the noonday sun; and there was no one there unappalled, O king, save the son of Somadatta.

sanskrit: sa hy ādadāno dhanur ugravegaṃ; bhūriśravā bhārata saumadattiḥ dṛṣṭvā rathān svān vyapanīyamānān; pratyudyayau sātyakiṃ yoddhum icchan
english: For Bhūriśravas, son of Somadatta, O Bhārata, taking up his bow of fierce force and seeing his own chariots borne away, went forth to meet Sātyaki, eager to fight.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato bhūriśravā rājan sātyakiṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ avidhyad bhṛśasaṃkruddhas tottrair iva mahādvipam
english: Saṃjaya said: Then Bhūriśravas, O king, in furious wrath pierced Sātyaki with nine arrows, as one goads a great elephant with hooks.

sanskrit: kauravaṃ sātyakiś caiva śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ avākirad ameyātmā sarvalokasya paśyataḥ
english: And Sātyaki of measureless spirit, in the sight of all the host, covered that Kaurava in turn with smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājā sodaryaiḥ parivāritaḥ saumadattiṃ raṇe yattaḥ samantāt paryavārayat
english: Then King Duryodhana, surrounded by his brothers, intent in battle, ringed the son of Somadatta about on every side.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavāḥ sarve sātyakiṃ rabhasaṃ raṇe parivārya sthitāḥ saṃkhye samantāt sumahaujasaḥ
english: In the same way all the Pāṇḍavas of mighty vigor stood encircling the impetuous Sātyaki on every side in the fray.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu saṃkruddho gadām udyamya bhārata duryodhanamukhān sarvān putrāṃs te paryavārayat
english: But Bhīmasena, kindled with wrath, raising his mace, O Bhārata, beset all your sons with Duryodhana at their head.

sanskrit: rathair anekasāhasraiḥ krodhāmarṣasamanvitaḥ nandakas tava putras tu bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam vivyādha niśitaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ kaṅkapatraiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: With many thousands of chariots, filled with wrath and indignation, your son Nandaka pierced the mighty Bhīmasena with six sharp heron-feathered shafts whetted on stone.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu samare bhīmasenaṃ mahābalam ājaghānorasi kruddho mārgaṇair niśitais tribhiḥ
english: And Duryodhana in battle, in his wrath, struck the mighty Bhīmasena upon the breast with three sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahābāhuḥ svarathaṃ sumahābalaḥ āruroha rathaśreṣṭhaṃ viśokaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Then the mighty-armed Bhīma of great strength mounted his own excellent chariot and spoke thus to Viśoka his charioteer:

sanskrit: ete mahārathāḥ śūrā dhārtarāṣṭrā mahābalāḥ mām eva bhṛśasaṃkruddhā hantum abhyudyatā yudhi
english: "These mighty car-warriors, the valiant and powerful sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, in their great wrath have risen up to slay me in the fight.

sanskrit: etān adya haniṣyāmi paśyatas te na saṃśayaḥ tasmān mamāśvān saṃgrāme yattaḥ saṃyaccha sārathe
english: This day I shall slay them all before your eyes, of that there is no doubt; therefore, O charioteer, hold my steeds well in hand and stay watchful in the battle."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tataḥ pārthaḥ putraṃ duryodhanaṃ tava vivyādha daśabhis tīkṣṇaiḥ śaraiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ nandakaṃ ca tribhir bāṇaiḥ pratyavidhyat stanāntare
english: So saying, the son of Pṛthā pierced your son Duryodhana with ten sharp gold-adorned arrows, and struck Nandaka in turn with three shafts between the breasts.

sanskrit: taṃ tu duryodhanaḥ ṣaṣṭyā viddhvā bhīmaṃ mahābalam tribhir anyaiḥ suniśitair viśokaṃ pratyavidhyata
english: But Duryodhana, having pierced the mighty Bhīma with sixty arrows, struck Viśoka in turn with three others keenly whetted.

sanskrit: bhīmasya ca raṇe rājan dhanuś ciccheda bhāsvaram muṣṭideśe śarais tīkṣṇais tribhī rājā hasann iva
english: And in the battle, O king, the king cut Bhīma's shining bow asunder at the grip with three sharp arrows, as though in mockery.

sanskrit: bhīmas tu prekṣya yantāraṃ viśokaṃ saṃyuge tadā pīḍitaṃ viśikhais tīkṣṇais tava putreṇa dhanvinā
english: But Bhīma, seeing his charioteer Viśoka there in the fight sorely beset by the sharp shafts of your bow-wielding son,

sanskrit: amṛṣyamāṇaḥ saṃkruddho dhanur divyaṃ parāmṛśat putrasya te mahārāja vadhārthaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: brooking it not and burning with wrath, laid hold of a celestial bow, O great king, O bull of the Bhāratas, to slay your son.

sanskrit: samādatta ca saṃrabdhaḥ kṣurapraṃ lomavāhinam tena ciccheda nṛpater bhīmaḥ kārmukam uttamam
english: In his fury he took up a feathered razor-edged shaft, and with it Bhīma cut asunder the king's excellent bow.

sanskrit: so 'pavidhya dhanuś chinnaṃ krodhena prajvalann iva anyat kārmukam ādatta satvaraṃ vegavattaram
english: Casting away his severed bow, blazing as it were with wrath, Duryodhana swiftly took up another bow of greater force.

sanskrit: saṃdhatta viśikhaṃ ghoraṃ kālamṛtyusamaprabham tenājaghāna saṃkruddho bhīmasenaṃ stanāntare
english: He fitted to it a dreadful arrow, bright as Time and Death, and with it in his wrath struck Bhīmasena between the breasts.

sanskrit: sa gāḍhaviddho vyathitaḥ syandanopastha āviśat sa niṣaṇṇo rathopasthe mūrchām abhijagāma ha
english: Pierced to the quick and racked with pain, he sank back into the body of his chariot, and there, seated in the chariot's seat, he fell into a swoon.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vyathitaṃ bhīmam abhimanyupurogamāḥ nāmṛṣyanta maheṣvāsāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ
english: Seeing Bhīma stricken thus, the great bowmen and mighty car-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas, with Abhimanyu at their head, could not endure it.

sanskrit: tatas tu tumulāṃ vṛṣṭiṃ śastrāṇāṃ tigmatejasām pātayām āsur avyagrāḥ putrasya tava mūrdhani
english: Then, calm and unflinching, they let fall a tumultuous rain of fierce-blazing weapons upon the head of your son.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ duryodhanaṃ tribhir viddhvā punar vivyādha pañcabhiḥ
english: Then the mighty Bhīmasena, recovering his senses, pierced Duryodhana with three arrows and again struck him with five.

sanskrit: śalyaṃ ca pañcaviṃśatyā śarair vivyādha pāṇḍavaḥ rukmapuṅkhair maheṣvāsaḥ sa viddho vyapayād raṇāt
english: And the great bowman of a Pāṇḍava pierced Śalya with twenty-five gold-feathered arrows; pierced thus, Śalya withdrew from the fight.

sanskrit: pratyudyayus tato bhīmaṃ tava putrāś caturdaśa senāpatiḥ suṣeṇaś ca jalasaṃdhaḥ sulocanaḥ
english: Then fourteen of your sons came forth to meet Bhīma — Senāpati and Suṣeṇa and Jalasaṃdha and Sulocana,

sanskrit: ugro bhīmaratho bhīmo bhīmabāhur alolupaḥ durmukho duṣpradharṣaś ca vivitsur vikaṭaḥ samaḥ
english: Ugra and Bhīmaratha and Bhīma and Bhīmabāhu and Alolupa, Durmukha and Duṣpradharṣa and Vivitsu and Vikaṭa and Sama.

sanskrit: visṛjanto bahūn bāṇān krodhasaṃraktalocanāḥ bhīmasenam abhidrutya vivyadhuḥ sahitā bhṛśam
english: Loosing many arrows, their eyes red with rage, they rushed upon Bhīmasena together and pierced him sorely.

sanskrit: putrāṃs tu tava saṃprekṣya bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ sṛkkiṇī vilihan vīraḥ paśumadhye vṛko yathā senāpateḥ kṣurapreṇa śiraś ciccheda pāṇḍavaḥ
english: But the mighty Bhīmasena, beholding your sons, licking the corners of his mouth like a wolf amid the flock, that hero, the Pāṇḍava, cut off the head of Senāpati with a razor-edged shaft.

sanskrit: jalasaṃdhaṃ vinirbhidya so 'nayad yamasādanam suṣeṇaṃ ca tato hatvā preṣayām āsa mṛtyave
english: Piercing through Jalasaṃdha, he sent him to the abode of Yama; then slaying Suṣeṇa, he dispatched him to Death.

sanskrit: ugrasya saśirastrāṇaṃ śiraś candropamaṃ bhuvi pātayām āsa bhallena kuṇḍalābhyāṃ vibhūṣitam
english: With a broad-arrow he struck to the ground the head of Ugra, helmet and all, fair as the moon and adorned with two earrings.

sanskrit: bhīmabāhuṃ ca saptatyā sāśvaketuṃ sasārathim nināya samare bhīmaḥ paralokāya māriṣa
english: And with seventy arrows Bhīma led Bhīmabāhu, together with his steeds, his banner, and his charioteer, to the other world in that battle, O sire.

sanskrit: bhīmaṃ bhīmarathaṃ cobhau bhīmaseno hasann iva bhrātarau rabhasau rājann anayad yamasādanam
english: The two impetuous brothers, Bhīma and Bhīmaratha both, Bhīmasena, as though in mockery, O king, sent to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: tataḥ sulocanaṃ bhīmaḥ kṣurapreṇa mahāmṛdhe miṣatāṃ sarvasainyānām anayad yamasādanam
english: Then in that great battle, before the eyes of all the troops, Bhīma sent Sulocana too to the abode of Yama with a razor-edged shaft.

sanskrit: putrās tu tava taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenaparākramam śeṣā ye 'nye 'bhavaṃs tatra te bhīmasya bhayārditāḥ vipradrutā diśo rājan vadhyamānā mahātmanā
english: But your sons, the others who remained there, seeing that prowess of Bhīmasena, were tormented with dread of Bhīma; and being slaughtered by that great soul, O king, they fled away in all directions.
